summary: Karl Eugen Neumann worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig University (~1887–1888) and under his doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel (~1888–1891).
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. From around 1856 to 1882, he held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served there as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from circa 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and under Ernst Windisch, Friedrich Max Müller, and Tetsujiro Inoue, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and Hamburg Colonial Institute (~1914–1935).

Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Hermann Brockhaus, Ernst Windisch, and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Tübingen (1876–1887), Halle (1887–1890), Berlin (1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1953), Harvard College (~1953–1956), and Harvard University (~1958–1966).

Karl H. Potter worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California (~1946–1950) and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1955), later serving as professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1970) and University of Washington (~1970–1997).

Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Indo-Iranian philology. He studied at the University of Munich under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, later holding chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar studied at the University of Vienna (1936–1941) and worked in archaeology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Weltmuseum Wien (~1947–1958), Mainz University (1961), and served as director at Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology after studying at Mainz (1787–1796) and Würzburg (1792–1796). He held posts at Lyceum Hosianum (1803), the Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1811), and the University of Bonn (1818).

Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics who studied at Leipzig University (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf, and held a professorship at the University of Göttingen starting in 1819.

Karl Popper studied philosophy at the University of Vienna (1918, ~1922–1928) and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Rosenkranz studied philosophy at Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, Heidelberg, and Halle. He held academic posts at the University of Halle (~1828–1833) and served as chair and rector at the University of Königsberg beginning in 1833.

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen (~1864–1873), and under August Leskien (~1871–1872). He served at the University of Halle library (~1876–1883) and Copenhagen as lecturer in Slavic studies (1882).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck, active in philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied at Augsburg and Munich. He held posts at the University of Munich (1978–1988), Munich School of Politics (1989–1991), and Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1975–1985) and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1992–1999). In 1999, he became a Privatdozent in Tibetology at Hamburg.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Anagarika Govinda from circa 1952 to 1985, later succeeding him from 1982 to 1999.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo studied under Tenzin Gyatso (~1972) and earned a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi (~1993–2000). She held posts at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and University of Hawaiʻi (2023).
